message.content:
**UNO – Quick‑Start Rules** | Step | What Happens | |------|--------------| | **1️⃣ Setup** | • Shuffle the standard UNO deck (108 cards).
• Deal each player 7 face‑up cards.
• Place the remaining deck facedown as the draw pile; flip its top card into an open “discard” stack next to it. If this first discard is a special action card, follow its effect immediately before play begins. | | **2️⃣ Turn Order** | Players sit clockwise around the table. The person who dealt starts and then turns proceed counterclockwise unless altered by a *Reverse* or *Skip*. | | **3️⃣ Playing a Card** | On your turn you may lay down one card from hand if it matches either:
- the color of the top discard OR
- the rank/value of the top discard (e.g., same number or symbol)
If no playable card exists, you must draw one from the draw pile. After drawing, if that new card can be played, you may do so right away; otherwise the turn ends. | | **4️⃣ Action Cards** | - **+2 / +4** : Next player draws two/four cards and forfeits their turn. (+4 requires proof that you had no matching colors.)
- **Draw Two** (`+2`) & **Wild Draw Four** (`+4`): Same as above but also skip the opponent’s turn.
- **Skip** : Opponent loses his/her upcoming turn.
- **Reverse** : Reverses direction of play (two players → Skip instead).
- **Wild** : You choose the new active color.
- **Wild Draw Four** : Choose color AND force next player to draw four cards plus lose a turn. Must only be used when you have no other legal move. | | **5️⃣ Winning a Round** | First player to empty their hand wins the round. They score points based on all cards left in opponents’ hands:
• Numbered cards count as their numeric value.
• Wild/Color Change = 50 pts.
• Reverse/Skip = 20 pts.
• Draw Two/Wild Draw Four = 30 pts. Add those totals to the winner’s cumulative score. | | **6️⃣ Game End** | Play continues until someone reaches at least **500 points**, though many groups set lower thresholds like 200 or 300. That player is declared overall champion. | --- ### Handy Tips - Keep track of which numbers/colors remain—this helps decide whether to use a `+4`. - When playing a `+4`, remember you’re allowed to challenge the previous player. If they were caught cheating, they’ll need to pick up eight cards! - In casual games, some house rules allow “draw three” or “wild reverse”; just agree beforehand. Enjoy! 🎉
